question: True or false: share markets in different countries move together more in crashes than in calm years?
answer: True. Longin and Solnik studied five large stock markets from 1959 to 1996 and found the links between them grow stronger in falling markets, not in rising ones. A spread that looks safe in calm years behaves like one bet exactly when protection is needed, as in 2008, when markets nearly everywhere fell together.
move: Things that seem separate in good times can fail together in bad ones.
ask: Are my safety nets truly separate, or would they all give way in the same bad year?
trap: False, because markets in separate countries look independent in normal years.
source: Longin and Solnik, Journal of Finance, 2001
reference: Longin & Solnik, Extreme Correlation of International Equity Markets, Journal of Finance, 2001
